q.t: What is a song's key?
q.e: A song in G mostly uses the notes of the G major scale, with G as home.

q.t: In Roman numerals, a capital numeral (like IV) means…
q.e: Capitals = major; small (like vi) = minor.

q.t: In the key of C, what is the I chord?
q.e: I is built on step 1 — the home chord.

q.t: In the key of C, what is the V chord?
q.e: Step 5 of C major is G.

q.t: In the key of C, what is the IV chord?
q.e: Step 4 of C major is F.

q.t: In the key of G, what is the I chord?
q.e: Home in G is G.

q.t: Which chord feels like 'home'?
q.e: I is the tonic chord — resting, finished.

q.t: Which chord creates tension that wants to go home?
q.e: V contains step 7, a half step below home, so it pulls back to I.

q.t: Which key is easiest for beginners because its main chords are all open chords?
q.e: G, Am, C, D, Em — all open chords.

q.t: The I – V – vi – IV progression in G is…
q.e: I = G, V = D, vi = Em, IV = C.

q.t: What is the pattern of chords in every major key?
o: Major, minor, minor, Major, Major, minor, dim
Major, Major, minor, minor, Major, minor, dim
minor, Major, Major, minor, minor, Major, dim
q.e: I ii iii IV V vi vii°.

q.t: In the key of C, what is the vi chord?
q.e: Step 6 is A; using only C-scale notes gives A C E = A minor.

q.t: In the key of C, what is the ii chord?
q.e: D F A — D minor.

q.t: In the key of G, what is the IV chord?
q.e: G A B C — step 4 is C.

q.t: In the key of G, what is the V chord?
q.e: Step 5 of G major is D.

q.t: In the key of G, what is the vi chord?
q.e: Step 6 of G is E; E G B = E minor.

q.t: The I – IV – V chords in the key of A are…
What is the relative minor of C major?
q.e: The vi chord. Am uses the same notes as C major.

q.t: What is the relative minor of G major?
q.e: vi of G is Em.

q.t: Why can a few chords be shared by thousands of songs?
o: Melody, rhythm and words make each song different
There are only four chords in music
q.e: The chords are the floor; what's built on top makes each song unique.

q.t: In the key of D, what are I, IV and V?
In the key of D, what is the vi chord?
q.e: Step 6 of D major is B; B D F♯ = B minor.

q.t: In the key of E, what is the V chord?
q.e: E F♯ G♯ A B — step 5 is B.

q.t: In the key of A, what is the vi chord?
q.e: A B C♯ D E F♯ — step 6 is F♯, which makes a minor chord.

q.t: Why is the ii chord in C (D F A) minor?
o: D → F is only 3 half steps
q.e: Using only C-scale notes, D to F is a minor 3rd.

q.t: Why is the V chord in C (G B D) major?
q.e: G to B is a major 3rd, so the chord is major.

q.t: Why does V pull back to I?
o: V contains step 7, a half step below home
V is always the last chord
q.e: In C, G contains B; B leans into C, so G → C sounds like coming home.

q.t: A song uses G, C, D and Em and ends on G. What key is it most likely in?
q.e: All four chords are in the G family, and it ends on G.

q.t: A song uses A, D, E and F♯m. What key is it most likely in?
q.e: All are in the A family: I, IV, V, vi.

q.t: G – D – Em – C and Em – C – G – D use the same chords. Why do they feel different?
o: Different starting chord sets a different 'home'
q.e: Starting on G (major) feels bright; starting on Em (relative minor) feels sad.

q.t: Using only C-scale notes, the chord built on B is B D F. Why is it 'diminished'?
o: B → F is 6 half steps, not 7
B is not in C major
q.e: A normal 5th is 7 half steps; B → F is only 6, so the 5th is 'diminished' (made smaller).

q.t: In the key of F (F G A B♭ C D E), what is the IV chord?
q.e: Step 4 of F major is B♭.

q.t: In the key of F, what is the V chord?
q.e: Step 5 of F major is C.

q.t: In the key of E, what is the iii chord?
q.e: E F♯ G♯ — step 3 is G♯, which makes a minor chord.

q.t: Which chord is not in the key of G?
q.e: G major has F♯, not F, so an F chord doesn't belong.

q.t: Which chord is not in the key of C?
q.e: D major needs F♯, which isn't in C major. Dm (D F A) is the ii chord.

q.t: Am is the relative minor of C. Which scale has the same notes as C major but starts on A?
q.e: A B C D E F G A — the natural minor scale on A.

q.t: What is the relative minor of D major?
q.e: vi of D is Bm (D E F♯ G A B).

q.t: What is the relative major of E minor?
q.e: Em is the vi of G, so G is its relative major.

q.t: A song in C stops on G and feels unfinished. Which chord would finish it?
q.e: G is V in C; it resolves to I — C.
